title: יהושע פרק 17
english: There was also a lot for the tribe of Manasseh; for he was the firstborn of Joseph; to wit, for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead: because he was a man of war, therefore he had Gilead and Bashan.

There was also a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families; for the children of Abiezer, and for the children of Helek, and for the children of Asriel, and for the children of Shechem, and for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida: these were the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph by their families.

But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, had no sons, but daughters: and these are the names of his daughters, Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

And they came near before Eleazar the priest, and before Joshua the son of Nun, and before the princes, saying, The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brethren. Therefore according to the commandment of the Lord he gave them an inheritance among the brethren of their father.
And there fell ten portions to Manasseh, beside the land of Gilead and Bashan, which were on the other side Jordan;
Because the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead.
And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem; and the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of Entappuah.
Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim;

And the coast descended unto the river Kanah, southward of the river: these cities of Ephraim are among the cities of Manasseh: the coast of Manasseh also was on the north side of the river, and the outgoings of it were at the sea:
Southward it was Ephraim's, and northward it was Manasseh's, and the sea is his border; and they met together in Asher on the north, and in Issachar on the east.

And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Bethshean and her towns, and Ibleam and her towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Endor and her towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and her towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and her towns, even three countries.
Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
Yet it came to pass, when the children of Israel were waxen strong, that they put the Canaanites to tribute, but did not utterly drive them out.
And the children of Joseph spake unto Joshua, saying, Why hast thou given me but one lot and one portion to inherit, seeing I am a great people, forasmuch as the Lord hath blessed me hitherto?

And Joshua answered them, If thou be a great people, then get thee up to the wood country, and cut down for thyself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the giants, if mount Ephraim be too narrow for thee.

And the children of Joseph said, The hill is not enough for us: and all the Canaanites that dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both they who are of Bethshean and her towns, and they who are of the valley of Jezreel.
And Joshua spake unto the house of Joseph, even to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, Thou art a great people, and hast great power: thou shalt not have one lot only:

But the mountain shall be thine; for it is a wood, and thou shalt cut it down: and the outgoings of it shall be thine: for thou shalt drive out the Canaanites, though they have iron chariots, and though they be strong.
ai_explanation: מנשה זכה בחלק נוסף מעבר לירדן כי הוא בכור יוסף; מכיר, אביו של הגלעד ומנהיגו שהיה איש מלחמה, קיבל את הגלעד והבשן.
שמות המשפחות המנויות — בני אביעזר, חֶלֶק, אשׂריאל, שֶׁכֶם, חֵפֶר ושְׁמִידָע — הם ראשי משפחות של בני מנשה.
לצלפחד בן חֵפר (בן גלעד, בן מכיר, בן מנשה) לא היו בנים אלא בנות, ושמות בנותיו הם מחלה, נועה, חגלה, מלכה ותירצה.

בנות צלפחד באו לפני אלעזר הכהן, יהושע וראשי העם וטענו שאלוהים ציווה למשה לתת להן נחלה בתוך אחיהן; הן זכו בנחלת אביהן כי הוא מת במדבר, הוכשר להן שיהיו נשואות בתוך שבטן כדי שלא תצא הנחלה מהשבט, והן נשאו לבני דודהן; וַיִּתֵּן להן ה' נחלה בתוך אחי אביהן.
למנשה נתרו עוד עשרה חבלי ארץ בנוסף לארץ הגלעד והבשן שמעבר לירדן.
בנות צלפחד משבט מנשה קיבלו נחלה בתוך נחלת בני השבטים, ובכך נוספו ארבעה חבלי ארץ על ששת חבלי משפחות מנשה; וארץ הגלעד הייתה לנחלת בני מנשה הנותרים.
גבול מנשה בארץ כנען נקבע מהמִכְמְתָת על פני שכם ועד ימינה אל יושבי עין תפוח.
למנשה הייתה ארץ תפּוח והשדות הסובבים אותה, ותפוח עצמה הייתה על גבול מנשה וקרובה לנחלת אפרים; כי מנשה ואפרים משבט אחד, נחלותיהם מעורבות.
הגבול ירד לנחל קנה: ערים אלה היו דרומית לנחל ושויכו לאפרים אך היו מבודדות בתוך ערי מנשה; גבול מנשה היה מצפון לנחל ויוצאיו היו אל הים.
נחל קנה שימש כגבול — דרומה לאפרים וצפונה למנשה; הים שימש גבולו של מנשה, ובנחלתו יגעו גבולות עם אשׁר מצפון ועם יששכר ממזרח.
למנשה היו חלקים בתוך נחלת יששכר ואשׁר, כולל ערים כמו בית שאן ויבלעם ועד מגידו עם כפריהן — אלה שלושת הנפתים שנמצאו שם.
בני מנשה לא יכלו לגרש את תושבי הערים המבוצרות האלו, ולכן הכנעני המשיך לשבת בארץ ההיא.
אחרי זמן החזיקו בני ישראל ונתנו את הכנעני לָמַס אך לא הורישו אותו; הכנענים נשארו בתוך נחלת שבט מנשה במשך דורות רבים.
בני יוסף פנו ליהושע וטענו שנחלת מנשה ואפרים נפלה בגורל אחד והתיחום ביניהן אינו ברור, והם עם רב ולכן השטח שהוקצה אינו מספיק להם וביקשו ברכה.
יהושע עונה שאם אתם רבים ויש לכם כוח — עלו ליער ובערו שם לעצמכם מקום בארץ הפריזי והָרפאים, כי הר־אפרים דחוק לכם; מבחינת השטח יש די מקום אם תכינו אותו.
בני יוסף השיבו שההר לא יספיק להם וכי בעמק, באזור בית־שאן ובעמק יזרעאל, יושבים כנענים מצוידים ברכב ברזל ולכן אינם יכולים להתמודד אתם שם.
יהושע אומר לבית יוסף — אתם עם רב וכוח גדול, ולכן לא תקבלו גורל אחד מצומצם.
יהושע מסביר שאפשר להרחיב את ההר כי הוא יער ולכן תכרו ותבראו אותו ותקבלו את תוצאתיו; ובסוף תורישו את הכנעני אף על פי שיש לו רכב ברזל וחוזק, ולכן אין צורך לתת לכם נחלה נוספת.
ai_explanation_en: Manasseh received an additional portion east of the Jordan because he was Joseph's firstborn through Machir; Machir, as a warrior, secured Gilead and Bashan for his descendants.
The remaining families of Manasseh each received a lot, and the named groups (Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, Shemida) were heads of families constituting the male households of Manasseh.
Zelophehad, a descendant of Manasseh through Hepher, had no sons but five daughters named Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

Zelophehad's daughters went before Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the leaders, asserting that God had commanded Moses to give them an inheritance among their father’s clan because their father died in the wilderness. They were instructed to marry within their tribe so the land would remain in Manasseh, and having already married their cousins they now sought an additional inheritance beyond what they held through their husbands; Joshua granted them the land according to God’s command.
Manasseh received ten portions in addition to the territories of Gilead and Bashan that lay across the Jordan.

Because Zelophehad’s daughters inherited within Manasseh, four extra territorial portions were added to the six family portions of Manasseh, while the land of Gilead belonged to the remaining sons of Manasseh.
Manasseh’s border in Canaan extended from the border of Asher to the place called Michmethah before Shechem, with the boundary running to the right toward the inhabitants of En-Tappuah.

Manasseh held the lands around Tappuah, but the town of Tappuah itself on Manasseh’s border belonged to the tribe of Ephraim; the two tribes’ inheritances were somewhat intermixed because both descend from Joseph.

The boundary descended to the Kanah stream, and the cities there are associated with Ephraim though they lie amid Manasseh’s towns; Manasseh’s territory lay north of the stream and its outlets were to the sea.

The Kanah stream served as the southern limit for Ephraim and the northern limit for Manasseh; the sea formed Manasseh’s western border, and its territory met Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

Manasseh held lands within the territories of Issachar and Asher, including cities such as Beth-shean, Ibleam, Dor, Endor, Taanach, and Megiddo with their surrounding districts — three regional districts in that area.
The men of Manasseh were unable to expel the inhabitants of those fortified cities, so the Canaanites continued to live in that land.

Steinsaltz notes that after some time, when the Israelites grew strong, they imposed tribute on the Canaanites but did not completely expel them; the Canaanites remained within the territory of the tribe of Manasseh for many generations.

He explains that the descendants of Joseph complained to Joshua because the inheritances of Manasseh and Ephraim fell as a single, somewhat ill-defined lot and boundary, and they claimed to be a large people whom God had blessed so that the allotted land was inadequate.

Joshua’s reply, as Steinsaltz renders it, is that if they are numerous and strong they have the power to expand: they should go up into the forested region and clear trees there in the lands of the Perizzites and Rephaim—if the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped, they can make more room.

The Joseph tribes answered that the hill country would not suffice because in the adjacent valley the Canaanites everywhere possess iron chariots—specifically those of Beth-shean and the Jezreel Valley—so they feel unable to contend with them.
Steinsaltz reports Joshua’s further assurance to Ephraim and Manasseh that, being a great and powerful people, they should not be confined to a single, limited allotment.

Finally, Steinsaltz explains Joshua’s point that the mountain will belong to them because it is wooded and can be cleared, its outlying parts will be theirs, and in time they will drive out the Canaanites despite their iron chariots and strength; therefore there was no need to grant them an additional inheritance.

did_you_know.text_en: The daughters appealed to both Eleazar the priest and to Joshua and the leaders — showing they brought their claim to religious as well as civic authorities.
